fluff.overview: The Ballista is a self-propelled artillery tank developed by Rivverson Technologies of Nanking during the late Age of War, entering service around 2480. Designed as a modernized indirect fire platform, the Ballista improved significantly on earlier artillery designs in mobility, crew protection, and operational flexibility. Lighter and faster than the bulky artillery pieces it replaced, it could deliver heavy indirect fire support while retaining the speed to relocate before counter-battery fire could respond. The vehicle established itself as the standard mobile artillery piece of the Star League era and proved economical and reliable enough to remain in active service across virtually every major military force, sustaining that role across multiple centuries of continuous use.
fluff.capabilities:
The Ballista's primary weapon is a Hegemony Arms DAT/91 Sniper artillery cannon mounted in a fully traversable turret, a defining feature that allows the vehicle to engage targets across multiple zones without repositioning the entire hull. Organized into batteries of four to six vehicles, a Ballista formation can sustain a continuous five-minute barrage before needing to reload, giving commanders a powerful tool for suppressing fortifications or breaking enemy concentrations. Three KKL/h-12 machine guns mounted in the hull provide the crew with direct-fire protection against infantry that might close under the artillery's minimum range.

The vehicle's PowerTech 165 HighLift internal combustion engine delivers a top speed just over fifty kilometers per hour, sufficient to execute rapid displacement between firing positions and support the shoot-and-scoot doctrine that keeps artillery crews alive. Seven and a half tons of Quantum Heavy Plate armor give the Ballista enough protection to survive most counter-battery fire and aerial strafing runs, though the vehicle cannot withstand direct engagement with heavier combat units for long. The tracked suspension allows it to cross virtually any terrain type with ease, an important quality for artillery that must constantly seek new positions to avoid retaliation.
fluff.deployment: The Ballista served in organized artillery batteries of four to six vehicles across every Star League nation and many Periphery states, fulfilling the standard indirect fire support role across all theaters. Its ease of maintenance, low operating costs, and reliable internal combustion engine made it a natural choice for reserve and garrison formations that could not be equipped with more modern artillery platforms. The vehicle remained a fixture of second-line units through the Amaris Civil War and into the early Succession Wars, a sign of the soundness of Rivverson's original design and the practicality that made it so widely imitated.
fluff.history:
Rivverson Technologies developed the Ballista during the latter half of the twenty-fifth century, drawing on manufacturing advances to produce a vehicle markedly superior to the artillery designs common during the Age of War. Where earlier self-propelled guns had been heavy, slow, and demanding of large crews, Rivverson's engineers created a platform that was lighter, faster, and better protected while requiring fewer operators to function effectively. The vehicle entered service around 2480 and quickly became the standard mobile field artillery piece for Terran Hegemony forces, with production based at the Nanking facility.

The design's effectiveness made it a natural candidate for imitation, and by the time of the Reunification Wars, dozens of virtual clone designs had appeared across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. When the SLDF absorbed regional forces during the Reunification, it inherited hundreds of clone variants built to varying standards, creating a logistical headache that persisted for decades. Nanking itself fell under Capellan Confederation control during the early Succession Wars, with production continuing for a time before the line went dark during the Late Succession Wars era as the Confederation lost the industrial capacity to maintain it.

Despite the factory's closure, the Ballista's story did not end at Nanking. By the twenty-eighth century the original had been superseded in first-line SLDF service by newer designs, but it remained a staple of reserve and garrison formations throughout the Amaris Civil War. The genuine article and its many clones continued seeing action during the Exodus Civil War and the Succession Wars that followed, with field-rebuilt examples and knock-offs manufactured throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery keeping the type in service long after Rivverson Technologies ceased producing the genuine article. The Ballista of the 2770s was still recognizably the same vehicle that had first rolled out of Nanking nearly three centuries earlier.
